findings.issue: The concurrency test does not prove the FOR SHARE guard. Its end-state assertions (CANCELLED, and SALE/COMMISSION/FEE all 0 or all 1) hold with or without the lock, because a booking made after the cancel leaves the same end state as one made before it. evidence.md confirms the test passed on base. It proves no deadlock and an all-or-nothing booking, nothing more.
findings.fix: Optional: add a deterministic interleaving test. Hold a FOR SHARE (or the cancel's row lock) in a test transaction, start the other side, assert it blocks, release, then assert the outcome. Or rename the test to say it only covers no-deadlock and atomicity.

findings.issue: On the legacy path, DELIVERED never calls track, so there may be no register row for FOR SHARE to lock. If a legacy CANCELLED insert has not committed yet, recordDelivered finds no row, does not wait, and books. The end state is CANCELLED plus booked, the AC-4 shape, so this is acceptable. But the comment on the lock in LedgerService ('never booked-after-cancel') overstates the guarantee for legacy orders.
findings.fix: Narrow the comment so the strict ordering guarantee covers only shipments that already have a register row (the parts path always tracks first). No code change needed.

findings.issue: Any event with no shipments and status CANCELLED now creates a register row keyed by orderId under the platform seller. order-service always sends o.shipments() (OrderEventPublisher.build), so this only happens for orders that really have no shipments. Collision with a real shipment is not a practical risk: OrderShipment ids come from @GeneratedValue(UUID), independent of the order id. The reconcile treats shipmentId == orderId as legacy and stays quiet on CANCELLED rows with no SALE. Still, an order cancelled with no shipments now leaves a register row that the reconcile keeps paging over.
findings.fix: None needed. Optionally note this in the method doc.

findings.issue: The 'shipment is cancelled' lookup repeats a ledger_shipments read that book() already did a few lines earlier (the currency read). .single() is safe there because that earlier read already required the row to exist.
findings.fix: Optional: read status and currency together once. Not required.

summary: The change is correct and minimal: about 35 production lines in seller-service, with no schema, endpoint or event change. Track's upsert now carries a terminal condition, 'ledger_shipments.status <> CANCELLED'; a CANCELLED row keeps its status, amount, seller and updated_at through replays, earlier statuses and unknown status text. recordDelivered's SELECT ... FOR SHARE is sound: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE takes a row lock that conflicts with FOR SHARE even when its WHERE is false, so a concurrent cancel waits for an in-flight booking, and a booking that starts while a cancel is uncommitted waits and re-reads the committed CANCELLED. Neither path can deadlock (track is REQUIRES_NEW and commits first; repair locks discrepancy then shipment, never the reverse). The legacy path (shipmentId = orderId, platform seller) matches legacy DELIVERED booking and the V3 backfill and cannot collide with generated shipment ids. The reconcile 409 follows the Q2 ruling and rolls back, leaving the discrepancy open (AC-11 test asserts both). The tests fail on their real assertions against base (8 failures in evidence.md); AC-8 and AC-9 are regression tests with a positive control. The only real gap is that the concurrency test cannot tell the lock is present.
